utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I mean, I came at noon or I came at midnight. I don't know if I came at noon, until when is my shift, until midnight, isn't it? And then the next shift comings on at midnight and so on. As a matter of fact, I don't know specifically if I -- my turn came at noon or at midnight, but I guess there were some changes there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps I can fit in one more question before the break, Mr. President. The name Vinko Skrobo, do you know where the name came from, the name of the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know much about it. It could have been, I don't know, Vinko Skrobo, who could have been a Croat soldier in some earlier time. I don't know. As far as I can remember. When, I really don't know. But he was a Croat soldier, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you, sir, that the name changed after you joined the unit, according to other evidence in the case, and I'm just -- you do not recall anything more about why the name was changed from Mrmak to Vinko Skrobo and who this person Vinko Skrobo was? Is that right? You just don't know anything more about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I've already told you that as far as I know, he was a Croat soldier. Vinko Skrobo was a Croat soldier, after whom would we name a unit if not after a Croat soldier? You don't think that we would name it after a Serb soldier or I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can break there, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 20 minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, please. Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, only briefly, I may not speak with the witness, so I have to tell you, could you please ask the witness how he's feeling? Because after you announced the break, the witness started and it was a bit slightly comic but it could also be tragic. He headed for the exit but the usher ran after him and caught him by the hand, not to prevent anyone from seeing who he is and I saw his face, which -- and I saw sheer horror on his face so I just thought, I don't know, perhaps could you ask him how he's feeling, and then we resume.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you were just saying right now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I'm fine. I'm saying. I was a little flustered, well, it doesn't matter, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to understand that all the measures we did is to protect your identity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] I know that [Interpretation] Yeah, I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just to inform the Chamber immediately after this incident took place I went to the room where the witness was and with the help of victims and witness section I explained to him exactly why we did that, and it wasn't anything but to protect him, so he understood and it was okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Scott, you may continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, before we move on to next couple of questions, you said before the break that Ernest Takac was your group or shift commander. I just want to clarify, did that continue to be the case from approximately the time you joined the unit in June, 1993, until at least the end of 1993, early 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I do not remember the very beginning. Later on, I think -- I think, yes, most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as the -- you've described for us this afternoon the way the shifts worked and that sort of thing. Where was Mr. Takac during the shift? Where was he positioned? Or what was his duty location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: It was all within that circle, within that position, and there was nothing fixed, nothing defined. Those shift leaders were not commanders properly speaking. I wouldn't say they had much authority -- they enjoyed much authority. You simply had a shift and you needed to have somebody there to have some order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And just again to be clear, when you say he was there within that circle, you mean he was at the health centre, around the location in the health centre, where you and others were serving your shift; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Yes. He'd be, for instance, at position 1, position 2, position 3, and so he moved about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving forward, then, you said that you were paid, and you told us a little bit about that. You were paid in cash throughout this time or how were you paid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: In the beginning, we were paid in cash, and later on, I am not sure when that was, I believe that several times, I don't know how many times, but for a while, we were getting money through the bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And focusing for a moment on the time when you were receiving cash, you understood, if I heard you correctly, sir, that the money was coming from -- the cash was being moved or transmitted from Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I have no direct knowledge about this but this is what I heard, that the money came from Grude. I'm telling our logistics man would go to Grude to get the cash and soldiers then came to the base to collect their salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before I come to him, focusing specifically on 1993, sir, and I'm not talking about the fighting earlier with the Serbs, I'm speaking very specifically about 1993, as far as you know, did the HVO in West Mostar have continuous access or freedom of movement to places such as Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: You mean 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I didn't quite -- you mean HVO soldiers or -- I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll repeat it, sir. As far as you know, did the HVO, by officers, by its officials, the ones located, for instance, in West Mostar, have continuous access to Grude and that region throughout 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Well, I guess so. Why not? Croats were not waging war against Croats, were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And for that very reason, sir, it's also fair to say, is it not, that the HVO in Mostar, in West Mostar, at least, had continuous access to the Republic of Croatia during 1993? Didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, who was this logistics man that you mentioned? You've mentioned him several times now. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: You mean the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Zeljko Colak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did he have that responsibility once again throughout the time that you were a member of the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And would it be this man who would actually physically distribute the cash to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have to sign something or make some sort of an record indicating that you had received your salary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't remember. Well, of course, I would have to sign something but I can't remember it in any detail. I mean whenever you collected your pay, of course you had to sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was your understanding of where this money was coming from? I mean physically, where was the cash, the currency, coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: You mean what notes, of which state? Of, shall I call it ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm just talking about the physical origin. I can ask you some other questions and may in a moment, but where did you understand the money that was coming, obviously the money had to be transported to the headquarters in West Mostar where you said you were paid. Where did you understand the money was physically coming from? Was it coming from Grude? Was it coming from some place else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I've already told you that the money, from what I heard, came from Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: How can I know what was it its original source? I'm no inspector, am I?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I was taking you back to Grude just to clarify -- I was talking about the physical movement of the money so that was my next question. Do you know how the money came to be in Grude? Perhaps you don't know but that's what I'm asking you. Do you know where this money came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I've no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was it Croatian dinars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Well, at that time, the Croatian dinar was the legal tender in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then later when you said that there came a time when it was changed where you were taking money in some fashion out of the bank, are you telling us that the money would be put on deposit in some bank in Mostar and then you could withdraw money from the bank? Is that the way it worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Well, I've told you, for a while, we drew that money from the bank, and -- but how can I know what were all these transactions? I'm not a financial expert to know these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course. But do you know, recalling the name of the bank and where it was located in Mostar that you could go during the war and take this money out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I believe it was so-called Splitska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I think I'm just going to skip over some questions for the sake of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to direct your attention forward a bit, please, from some of the other times we have been talking about to the 30th of June, to the 4th of July, 1993. And do you recall were you on duty, as you've described it to us today, were you on duty at the health centre on those days? At a time when -- if it will assist you, sir, when the ABiH had attacked what was called the Northern Barracks and then there was a furthers wave of arrests of Muslims that puts the -- marks the time in your mind. During those days, where were you and what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I was at home, or I could have been somewhere, say, near the base, in a pub or somewhere. I don't know, but I remember when there was this gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is your recollection that you were not in fact on duty during that time at all? During that approximate, say, four or five days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Well, I was on duty one of those days but on any specific day, where I was and what I was doing, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, during that time, sir, did you participate in arresting any Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And during that time, sir, did you participate in expelling any Muslims from their homes or flats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you steal or loot any property from any Muslims during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Never. I'm, as people call it, an anti-materialistic kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that nobody in the Vinko Skrobo unit did any of those things during early July, 1993, that it simply didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone, and if somebody did it, well, that's his problem, because I can't see everybody. Our task was to guard the fortified lines and some individual, an individual, went home after he'd done his duty, I didn't watch over them to see what they were doing then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you, direct your attention, please to another time and ask you similar questions. I know this is sometime ago. Do you recall whether you were on duty toward the end of September, 1993, approximately the 29th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Who can remember that? Who can remember that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, during that time, sir, late September, 1993, again I ask you did you arrest any Muslims during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you participate in expelling any Muslims from their homes or flats during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I've already said it, I never participated in any of these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I heard you on direct examination, sir, you did say, you did ultimately confirm that you were aware the Muslims civilians were being expelled from West Mostar during this time. Did I hear you correctly n general, I'm talking the summer and the fall of 1993. Did I hear you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: It wasn't something that was widely known. I heard those stories. I did not see any such case. One knew that there were expelled, that it is a fact some people were expelled but who did it, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, the allegation, at least, is that these -- that there were times when these were not one or two individual Muslims being expelled but there were large numbers of Muslims being expelled from particular neighbourhoods. Are you telling the Judges that you just never heard about that or that you had no information at all that this was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question once again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I put it to you, sir, if I can put it -- I'll state it that way. I put it to you that there were a number of instances throughout the summer and fall of 1993 when large numbers of Muslim families were expelled, not just one individual here and another individual two weeks later. But large scale expulsions. Is it your position, is it your testimony, that you did not know these things were happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I did know of that, that certain groups of Muslims were expelled, but specifically, I did not participate in any such acts, and I didn't see anyone doing it. As I was saying, I was a soldier who did his duty on the front line, after the front line I went home. I did my work, my own work, or I was in company with some friends. I was not interested in anything else but protecting the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Turning to Muslim prisoners who came to the headquarters area or the health centre area during this time, did I understand you correctly, sir, to be talking -- giving your testimony about a group of something -- from perhaps five to -- another time I think you said ten to 15, prisoners, who were actually from the neighbourhood? Is that the only group of prisoners that you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: As far as I know that group was mostly the same, the auto mechanics were always the same. Now, maybe among the other prisoners, there may have been changes. I don't know. I don't remember any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, is it fair to say, I just want to be sure we you will understand your testimony, would it be fair to say that when counsel asked you about the way the prisoners were treated, and the conditions in which they were held, it was that particular group of prisoners that you were talking about, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Yes. They were mostly this same group of prisoners, as I was saying, who, as I was saying, were our acquaintances or some other soldier knew them and they felt safer to spend the night there sometimes. They had good conditions. They did light work and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did decide during the break to show the witness one exhibit that's already in evidence but if I could just put it on the ELMO, it might be the easiest thing. It's Exhibit P633. It will not disclose in any way the identity of the witness so I don't think there is any reason why it can't be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, again, I'm caught by surprise by a document that is going to be used in the cross-examination. This has become frequent now and I don't think it is by chance. And we don't have a carriage or the ability to carry all these documents with us into the courtroom to be able to find them easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's now very difficult to judge whether the Prosecution is doing this purposely or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can give you, I think respectfully, Mr. President, I think I can give you what I hope will be a persuasive answer. It was until cross-examination, I believe, and I just was trying to confirm this with Mr. Bos, it was not until cross-examination that we heard that Mr. Takac was this man's commander, and it was based upon learning that information for the first time that I recalled a particular exhibit. Which is already admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since this document will be put on the ELMO, and everybody in this courtroom has a chance to look at it, I don't think that will be prejudice to the rights of the Defence. So we may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at the Croatian language version where and if the English version could be placed on the ELMO, please? This is a statement allegedly given by Mr. Martinovic concerning an incident on the 6th of October, 1993. My first question to you, sir, as you look at that is, do you recall this incident of a gun fight between the -- members of the Vinko Skrobo unit and members of the Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I know that there was an incident, but I didn't participate and I don't know any specific details. I know that there was tension between them for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, again I'm going to put to you that, unless these sorts of things happened every day, this must have been a rather notorious and well known incident, especially if it involved your group commander, Mr. Takac. Isn't that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: As I was saying, I'm not familiar with the details. I know that a conflict broke out. I simply wasn't present, nor did I engage in anything outside protecting the line. I can't tell you anything specific about that. I can't make up anything when I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just point out one particular part to you and I'll ask you a question or two and then we will move on. I'm looking, sir, at the part immediately below "statement."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to continued questioning about this document because the witness said that he had nothing to do with this document, that he has no idea about it, that he's not familiar with the incident. Therefore any further examination of this witness on this document is really inappropriate and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness said that he was not familiar with the details, but he knows that a conflict broke out. Let us see what the witness knows about this incident, about this conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm directing your attention to the part that begins immediately after the section heading called "statement." It says, "At about 2145 hours, on 6 October, 1993, General Andabak's driver Zoran by name came to our base and told me that I had to report urgently to Mr. Tuta at the tobacco depot in Siroki Brijeg. I immediately sat at the wheel of my Buick and beside me was one of my soldiers, Ernest Takac. As we were setting off, one of the lads --" I'll let you continue on. You can see certain names that you name recognise, the name Baja, the name Semir Bosnjic and looking at that statement, sir, to the extent whatever memory you have of that incident, is that consistent with what you heard and what people were saying around the base about this incident at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I said earlier on that I had heard of this conflict and as I was saying, what actually happened, the details, and surely it's normal, even in peace time for people to clash, never mind in wartime. It's nothing unusual. I don't see what the fuss is about this. I don't know any specific details. I repeat once again, I just heard that there was a conflict. What, how and when, I really don't know. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I allow that these kinds much events perhaps became common to you, to most of us perhaps a gun fight between two units on the same side would be something that might be memorable. Mr. Takac, for instance, after this event, as you were manning a shift, a 12 hour shift at the health centre, there was no conversation about, "Boy you should have seen what happened the other day? We had a real gunfight with those guys. It was really a bad situation." You don't remember any conversations like that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to object, Mr. President. Is this a question or is this testimony on the part of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It is a question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think it is a question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Could you repeat it once again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll simplify it sir, it's your testimony that you don't recall any conversations about this incident, after the fact, discussion among your colleagues, discussions with Mr. Takac, it's simply dropped -- the subject simply dropped and you don't remember anything more about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: As I was saying, there was some talk about a conflict, as for shooting, any details, I really don't remember. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, one final question, sir, and then I'll --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: It wasn't really -- I don't know, as I was saying, what the fuss is about over this incident. It wasn't any special occurrence. I don't see anything special about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, did either Mr. Martinovic or Mr. Takac, around this time, explain or ever say anything about why it was that Stela had to report urgently to Mr. Tuta in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Did I say that Stela reported to Tuta in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, sir, I read the statement to you and my question to you now is: You don't have any recollection or you can not provide any assistance to the Chamber why it was that Mr. Martinovic and Mr. Takac had to report urgently that day to Mr. Tuta at the tobacco station in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. My duty was to protect the already-fortified lines and those private affairs or whatever one likes to call them, these other things, outside protection of the line, simply did not interest me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my final --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, you see that I'm trying to avoid comments, objections and everything else, but Your Honours, in the cross-examination, when five times a witness says that he doesn't know something, do we really have to, for the sixth time, insinuate to the witness something that he has said for five times that he doesn't know anything about it? So surely cross-examination should be correct examination and not insinuations within questions. That's all I wanted to say. Thank you. For the transcript, for the record, and I apologise. I know we are all tired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this witness is not your witness. It's Mr. Seric's witness. And Mr. Seric has rightly raised his objection during the cross-examination. And I believe that the party conducting the cross-examination has the right to do everything possible to refresh the memory of the witness. I think they are entitled to do that. You may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my final question to you or two, depending on your answer, is: You said on direct examination, when asked about whether this man Halil Ajanic considered Stela responsible for the death of his son, you said you -- if I heard you correctly, sir, you said you first heard that "the other day." Can you tell us, sir, how it was that you heard this information the other day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. I think it was in the plane, somebody said, one of these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, who told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. Maybe everybody said it. I have no idea, no clue. There was talk about this and that is how I learned about it. Only thing, that Halil had accused Stela, and I was surprised, because I know almost everything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, to be cautious, we should probably go to private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, did you see or hear, personally, in that -- Mr. Ajanic's statement, that was reproduced on BH television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MN
utterances.text: I've only heard about this incident and I was really surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from Judges? No? Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming here to give your evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. We all the wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, are there any documents to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. It is the plan of the town, D2/39 and the photograph which was marked by the witness, where he marked where the tank moved and those obstacles put there, D2/40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So they are admitted into evidence and the D2/39 is under seal. Well, after four and a half months, I think everybody in this room deserves some rest so we will break now until the videolink. And this bench will issue our order concerning the arrangement of the videolink. We will rise until the 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 4.25 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 26th day of August, 2002, at 9.30 a.m.
